reference.source: Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics / relevant specialty textbook
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive chromosomal-instability disorder caused by biallelic variants in BLM, encoding a RecQ-family DNA helicase
Marked pre- and postnatal proportionate growth restriction with a characteristically small, narrow face is a defining feature
A sun-sensitive telangiectatic erythematous rash develops over the face, often in a butterfly distribution, and on other exposed areas
There is a very high lifetime risk of a broad range of malignancies at unusually young ages, spanning leukaemias, lymphomas and many solid tumours
Immunodeficiency predisposes to recurrent respiratory and ear infections, and there is a high rate of type 2 diabetes and reduced fertility
The diagnostic laboratory hallmark is a greatly increased rate of sister chromatid exchange on cytogenetic testing
There is heightened sensitivity to DNA-damaging agents and ionising radiation, so diagnostic radiation and certain chemotherapies must be used cautiously
reference.pathophysiology: Bloom syndrome is caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in BLM, which encodes a RecQ-family DNA helicase essential for maintaining genomic stability during DNA replication and repair, particularly in resolving recombination intermediates and stalled replication forks. Loss of BLM function leads to excessive homologous recombination and a striking increase in sister chromatid exchanges, the cytogenetic signature of the disorder. This genomic instability drives the profound cancer predisposition and contributes to the growth failure and other systemic features. The condition is more frequent in the Ashkenazi Jewish population owing to a founder variant.
additionalDifferentials: Fanconi anaemia and other chromosomal-instability syndromes
Cockayne syndrome and other photosensitivity disorders
Russell-Silver syndrome and other primordial growth-restriction disorders
additionalInvestigations: Cytogenetic sister chromatid exchange assay demonstrating a markedly elevated exchange rate
Molecular genetic testing of the BLM gene to confirm biallelic variants
Full blood count and immunoglobulin levels to assess immunodeficiency
Fasting glucose and glycaemic testing for diabetes
Age- and symptom-directed cancer surveillance imaging and endoscopy
redFlags: Symptoms or signs suggesting a new malignancy, which may arise at any site and at a young age
Recurrent or severe infections indicating significant immunodeficiency
Unexpected severe toxicity following radiation or DNA-damaging chemotherapy
Failure to thrive with progressive growth failure in infancy
reference.prognosis: Life expectancy is significantly reduced, largely because of the exceptionally high and early risk of multiple cancers, which are the leading cause of death. Infections, diabetes and chronic pulmonary disease add to morbidity, and management is supportive with intensive cancer awareness and cautious use of DNA-damaging treatments.
pitfalls: Using standard-dose radiotherapy or DNA-damaging chemotherapy without accounting for the extreme treatment sensitivity
Attributing early growth restriction to nutritional causes and missing the underlying diagnosis
Failing to maintain a low threshold for investigating possible malignancy
Overlooking associated immunodeficiency and diabetes in ongoing care
references: Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics
management: No disease-specific therapy exists; care centres on intensive, age-directed cancer surveillance for the leukaemias, lymphomas and solid tumours that arise unusually early
Use radiotherapy and DNA-damaging (alkylating and radiomimetic) chemotherapy with great caution and dose reduction because of the profound cellular hypersensitivity
Strict photoprotection with sun avoidance and sunscreen for the sun-sensitive telangiectatic facial rash
Prompt treatment of recurrent respiratory and ear infections, with assessment and support of the associated immunodeficiency including immunoglobulin therapy where indicated
Screening for and management of type 2 diabetes, with nutritional support for the growth failure
Autosomal recessive genetic counselling and family and carrier testing, noting the Ashkenazi Jewish founder variant
